column1: # 亚细亚三重奏 — what the coloured mini-diagrams actually are.
# A marker sits centred above ONE character cell and draws that character's
# READING, in the same room-partition style as the big black diagrams:
#   Chinese panel (left)        pinyin: one box per LETTER (17w x 25h, taller
#                               than wide).  A box split into a small top strip
#                               + a larger bottom = a letter that carries a dot
#                               or diacritic (i, j, or a tone-marked vowel).
#   Korean panel (top right)    hangul: one 35x35 square = one syllable; the
#                               2 boxes on top + 1 wide below, or left column
#                               split + right column = vertical vowel + 종성.
#   Japanese panel (bottom rt)  kana: one 17x17 square per kana of the reading.
# Coloured boxes = the pieces that travel.  Each panel's FOOTER draws the string
# assembled from the PREVIOUS panel in the cycle, same style and same scale:
#   Chinese pinyin -> Korean panel footer   (boxes 17w x 26h = letters)
#   Korean hangul  -> Japanese panel footer (boxes 35x35   = syllables)
#   Japanese kana  -> Chinese panel footer  (boxes 17x17   = kana; one half-size
#                                            box at the baseline = a SMALL kana)
